properties.name: A status that moves past its own prose says so, in the reply that moved it
properties.rationale:
OPTION A OF AN IDEA THE GRAPH ALREADY HELD, AND I DID NOT FIND IT BEFORE BUILDING. dec:idea-a-status-that-advances-past-its-own-prose was captured 2026-09-02 from the same dev_storyflow report and turned over four options; this is its option A, chosen by Anthony on 2026-09-04. I recorded the defect afresh this session and met the existing idea only when the duplicate guard surfaced it on the capability write, AFTER the code was built and tested.

THAT MISS IS THE LESSON, AND IT IS A THIRD KIND OF SEARCH. dev_storyflow named two in the same batch: the duplicate search looks for nodes that say the same thing, the premise search looks for nodes that say the opposite. This is a third - the SAME PROBLEM recorded under a different ACT. I searched for the defect's wording; the graph held the idea's wording. Nothing was wasted, since the build matches option A, but four options were re-derived from scratch and option D's counter-argument was already written down.

IT ALSO CORRECTS A CLAIM MADE HOURS EARLIER. fact:five-of-nine-field-entries-were-already-shipped-before-triage closes with NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the v0.47.0 triage already read the three 2026-09-02 entries. It is now established for at least one: that decision node IS that reading, dated 2026-09-02.

WHY A REPLY AND NOT A DETECTOR, which is the reporter's argument and the decision's option A: a set_status call already knows the description was not touched, because changing the status is the whole of what it does. No gap, no nudge, no sweep - it speaks at the moment the divergence is created, while the author is still in the room. Its stated limit is inherited from the decision: it reaches only the agent making that call, so prose that rots because the WORLD moved is untouched.

THE FEATURE CAUGHT ITSELF IN THE FIELD DURING THIS SESSION. Marking the verification that pins it from planned to passing returned a prose_currency block quoting that verification's own description - the first live firing, on the check that pins it.

AND THIS CALL DEMONSTRATED THE ABSORBED-MARKUP GUARD. The first attempt swallowed this very rationale into the summary; the reply said so by name and told me to re-send. That guard is exactly what dev_storyflow asked for on 2026-08-23 and it already exists on this path - which is why the same slip was silent four times on add_decision and add_capability and loud once here.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: New module crates/reflow2-mcp/src/prose_currency.rs, wired into set_capability_status, set_verification_status and set_epoch_status. When a status ACTUALLY MOVES and the node carries prose, the reply gains a prose_currency block: the field, the status the prose was written under, the status now, a 240-character excerpt cut on a char boundary, and a sentence asking whether it still reads true. Silent when the status did not move, and silent when there is no prose. All three tool descriptions were extended to say the block exists, so the feature has an instruction leg and not only a code one. Pinned by ver:a-status-advance-says-whether-its-prose-predates-it: 4 probes, observed failing first, with both counterweights correctly staying green against the neutered build. Also fixes three runs of eighteen literal spaces in the required-fields refusal at service.rs:368 - the same class as the served sentence repaired this morning, and found by pointing this session's new whitespace invariant at a message it was not written for.
